text: Context is crucial. <break time="0.8s" /> To the proper interpretation and understanding of linguistic utterances. <break time="0.8s" /> And a careful thinker ought to keep in mind. <break time="0.8s" /> The possibility of drawing potentially misleading interpretations from a passage. <break time="0.8s" /> If no attention is given. <break time="0.8s" /> To possible differences in context, intention, vocal emphasis, and punctuation. <break time="0.8s" /> In fact we should keep in mind. <break time="0.8s" /> That even the literal truth can sometimes be used. <break time="0.8s" /> To deceive or mislead. <break time="0.8s" /> In explaining some of the differences. <break time="0.8s" /> Between British and American conceptions of justice. <break time="0.8s" /> For instance. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom Cowan tells the story of a sea captain. <break time="0.8s" /> Confronted with the question of what to do about a mate. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose love for the bottle was getting out of control. <break time="0.8s" /> At last after one too many mishaps. <break time="0.8s" /> The captain had no choice. <break time="0.8s" /> But to state on the ships log. <break time="0.8s" /> The mate was drunk today. <break time="0.8s" /> The mate was not too pleased. <break time="0.8s" /> With this turn of events. <break time="0.8s" /> And so on a day. <break time="0.8s" /> When it was his turn to write on the ships log. <break time="0.8s" /> He took his revenge. <break time="0.8s" /> And recorded on the log. <break time="0.8s" /> The captain was sober today.
